passage: In the school yard in Accra, Kofi walked around the long way so he would not pass Dalia's class. Last Friday he had promised to help her paint the set for the play, but he went to play football instead and never said a word. Now his ears burned whenever he saw her. All week he hid behind the water tank at lunch. On Thursday he saw her holding a heavy board alone, and his stomach turned. He walked across the yard and said, "I did not come because I chose football. I am sorry. Can I paint with you now?" Dalia looked at him for a moment and handed him a brush.

qa.q: Which city is the school in?
Why did Kofi avoid Dalia's class and hide behind the water tank?
qa.a: He was embarrassed and ashamed for breaking his promise to help paint the set.

qa.q: What did Kofi do that started to repair things?
qa.a: He told her the truth, said sorry and offered to paint with her, instead of hiding any longer.

qa.q: How might Dalia have felt when Kofi finally came over?
qa.a: Dalia may have felt let down earlier and cautious, but she seemed willing to accept the honest apology, since she handed him a brush.

grounding: A child ashamed of breaking his promise hides for a week, then tells his friend the truth, apologises and offers to make it up.

passage:
'Hrithik! Why are you hiding behind the notice board?'
Hrithik winced. 'I'm not hiding.'
'You've avoided me for three days.' Hansa folded her arms. 'You promised to help me practise my elocution speech on Sunday. I waited at the park for an hour.'
His face burned. He had gone to his cousin's cricket match instead and forgotten. Every time he saw her, the shame got worse.
'I... I forgot. I went to a match. I'm really sorry, Hansa. I was too embarrassed to say it.'
She was quiet. 'You could have just told me.'
'I know. Can I make it up? The contest's next Friday. I'll listen to your speech every day at lunch this week.'
Hansa sighed. 'Every day?'
'Every single day.'
'Fine. Starting now.'

qa.q: How long did Hansa wait at the park?
Why had Hrithik been hiding from Hansa?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and embarrassed about breaking his promise, and the shame grew each time he saw her.

qa.q: How did Hrithik start to repair things?
qa.a: He told the truth, apologised, and offered to hear her speech every day at lunch.

qa.q: How did Hansa feel about being avoided?
qa.a: Hurt and annoyed; she would rather he had simply told her.

grounding: A boy too embarrassed to face the friend whose promise he broke finally tells the truth, apologises and makes up for it.

passage: Last term I promised Shalini I'd be her partner for the dance competition. Then the most popular girl in class asked me, and I said yes without thinking. I'm Jasleen, and I spent a week hiding from Shalini, going to the library at lunch and taking the other staircase. My stomach felt heavy every time I saw her plait at the end of the corridor. Hiding just made it bigger. Finally I wrote her a note: 'I broke my promise because I wanted to look cool. That was wrong. I'm sorry.' I slipped it into her bag and waited, feeling sick. The next day she found me. 'It hurt,' she said. 'But thanks for being honest.' After that I helped her practise with her new partner every afternoon.

qa.q: Where did Jasleen go at lunch to hide?
What did Jasleen's heavy stomach show?
qa.a: Jasleen felt ashamed and guilty about breaking the promise to Shalini.

qa.q: What finally started to heal things?
qa.a: Writing Shalini an honest note that admitted the real reason and said sorry, then helping her practise.

qa.q: How did Shalini feel about the broken promise and the note?
qa.a: Hurt by the broken promise, but thankful that Jasleen was honest.

grounding: A child hides from a friend after breaking a promise, then admits the truth in a note and makes amends.
